title: Balanced Brackets
statement:
Check whether the brackets in a string are balanced, using your language's standard stack or deque. A string is balanced when every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket of the same kind, and the pairs close in the right order, so `([])` is balanced but `([)]` is not.

The input is one line made only of the characters `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{`, and `}`. The line may be empty, and an empty line counts as balanced. Print `true` when the brackets are balanced and `false` otherwise.

Input:

```text
{[()()]}
```

Expected output:

```text
true
```
hints: Push every opening bracket onto a stack. The most recent unclosed bracket is always on top.
A closing bracket must match the bracket on top of the stack. It fails when the stack is empty or the kinds differ.
At the end, the string is balanced only if the stack is empty again.
